بودجهٔ سالانهٔ دولت سالانه شش کرور (و نیم) تومان کسری داشت و کمیسیون مجلس دو راه‌حل را در نظر گرفت: یکی افزودن بر درآمد دولت و دیگری کاستن از دریافت‌ها (دررفت‌ها).

- درآمد دولت پانزده کرور تومان و نیم و دررفت آن بیست و یک کرور تومان و نیم بود که سالانه شش کرور کم می‌داشت و می‌بایست جای آن با وام پر شود (گفتار چهارم، شاهد ۱).
- مجلس کمسیونی برای این کار برگزید که یکی از اعضای آن وثوق‌الدوله بود (گفتار چهارم، شاهد ۲ و ۳).
- دو راه چاره: «یکی آنکه بدرآمد افزایند، و دیگری اینکه از دریافت بکاهند» (گفتار چهارم، شاهد ۳).
- از جمله راه‌های افزایش درآمد، افزودن «تفاوت عمل» (فزونی مالیات‌های حکمرانان) به حساب دولت بود (شاهد ۳).
- کمیسیون مالی از راه کاهش دررفت‌ها، سالانه هشت کرور کم کرد، مثلاً با کاستن از مستمری شاهزادگان (گفتار هشتم، شاهد ۴).

بند سابله را شیخ سلمان در جلوی کارون بست تا آب رود را بالا آورده به جوی قبان و سپس به رشته جوی‌های دیگر سرازیر کند و زمین‌های بخش جنوبی خوزستان را چند فرسنگ فاریاب و آباد گرداند [2]. تاریخ زندیه آن را «نمونه سد اسکندر» نامیده است [3]. کریم‌خان در لشکرکشی به خوزستان این بند را بشکست، کاری که مؤلف آن از سیاه‌کاری‌های کریم‌خان می‌شمارد، زیرا بندبانی استواری که مایه سرسبزی فرسنگ‌ها زمین بود برافتاد [3]. میجر کینیرا نیز نوشته اگر کریم‌خان آن را نشکسته بود تا قرن‌ها استوار می‌ماند [1]. پس از آن شیخ سلمان در مدت پنج سالی که زنده بود دیگر به بستن بند برنخاست و آبادی‌های نتیجه آن بند یکبار دیگر از میان رفت [6]. بنیاد آن بند به نوشته مؤلف تذکره چوب و نی خاشاک بوده است [1].

Yes, force is allowed in the bridge case. According to Chapter V (Applications), if a public officer or anyone else sees a person attempting to cross a bridge ascertained to be unsafe, and there is no time to warn him of the danger, they may seize him and turn him back. This does not really infringe his liberty, because liberty consists in doing what one desires, and he does not desire to fall into the river. However, when there is not a certainty but only a danger of mischief, no one but the person himself can judge the sufficiency of the motive prompting him to incur the risk; so, unless he is a child, delirious, or in some state of excitement or absorption incompatible with the full use of the reflecting faculty, he ought only to be warned of the danger, not forcibly prevented. Finally, Mill says in Chapter I (Introductory) that the doctrine applies only to human beings in the maturity of their faculties — not to children or young persons below the legal age, who must be protected against their own actions as well as external injury.

Darwin calls it the doctrine of Malthus applied to the whole animal and vegetable kingdoms [3], [5].

- Malthus states that population, when unchecked, increases in a geometrical ratio, while subsistence increases only in an arithmetical ratio (Chapter 1) [1].
- Because food is necessary to life, the effects of these unequal powers must be kept equal, producing a strong check on population from the difficulty of subsistence (Chapter 1) [1].
- As his rule, Malthus takes the doubling of population every twenty-five years, based on the experience of the United States, where subsistence was ample and checks to early marriage few (Chapter 2) [2].

On Liberty (Mill) - Chapter I: society's tyranny penetrates much more deeply into the details of life and enslaves the soul itself, imposing prevailing opinion and feeling as rules of conduct on dissenters by means other than civil penalties.
Democracy in America (Tocqueville) - Chapter XVI: the effects of the tyranny of the majority are more sensibly felt in the manners than in the conduct of society, checking the development of leading characters.

Both see the danger reaching beyond laws and officials into social life itself: Mill emphasizes the tyranny of prevailing opinion and feeling enslaving the soul, while Tocqueville emphasizes its effects on manners and the suppression of independent, leading characters.

Veblen concedes that the corset impairs the personal attractions of the wearer, but this loss is offset by the gain in reputability that comes from her visibly increased expensiveness and infirmity (Chapter Seven, evidence [1]).

The corset has fallen into disuse among the richest class because a leisure class has grown up with such wealth that any aspersion on the score of enforced manual employment would be idle and harmless calumny (evidence [3], [5]).

It persists among some wealthy groups because they have not yet had time to divest themselves of the plebeian canons of taste and reputability carried over from their former, lower pecuniary grade — for example, the higher social classes of American cities that have recently and rapidly risen into opulence, during the period of snobbery and transition (evidence [2], [3]).

On Liberty (Mill) - United States: the feeling of the majority, to whom any appearance of a more showy or costly style of living than they can hope to rival is disagreeable, operates as a tolerably effectual sumptuary law, making it difficult for a person with a very large income to find any mode of spending it that will not incur popular disapprobation.
The Theory of the Leisure Class (Veblen) - motive: the accepted standard of expenditure in the community or class largely determines a person's standard of living, enforced through popular insistence on conformity to the accepted scale of expenditure as a matter of propriety, under pain of disesteem and ostracism.

Mill describes majority feeling in the United States acting as a sumptuary law that restrains conspicuous, showy spending by the very wealthy; Veblen's theory explains the restrained motive as the drive to display costly expenditure to meet the community's accepted pecuniary standard of living, conformity to which is enforced by fear of disesteem and ostracism.

No — both fail under the GDPR.

- Recital guidance in Regulation (EU) 2016/66 states that silence, pre-ticked boxes or inactivity should not constitute consent; consent requires a clear affirmative action or statement (evidence [1]).
- Article 7 requires that it be as easy to withdraw consent as to give it, so a letter-only withdrawal requirement is not acceptable (evidence [2]).
- Article 13 also requires informing the data subject of the right to withdraw consent at any time (evidence [3]).
- The Digital Markets Act recitals reinforce that consent must be given by clear affirmative action and that withdrawing it must be possible in an explicit, clear and straightforward manner (evidence [6]).

Yes — the retailer's use is caught, while the lab's original research use is not.

- Recital 25 excludes from the Regulation's scope AI systems specifically developed and put into service for the sole purpose of scientific research and development [1].

Under section 22(3), the time limit is the end of 30 days beginning with the first day after ownership/possession transfer, delivery, and any required installation or notification, so ten weeks exceeds it (section 22(1)). The next remedy is the right to repair or replacement under section 23, and then the right to a price reduction or the final right to reject under section 24, as set out in section 19(3) for goods not of satisfactory quality (a breach of section 9). On proof, section 19(14) provides that goods not conforming within six months of delivery are presumed not to have conformed on the delivery day, so the consumer need not prove the fault existed at delivery, unless the trader establishes the goods did conform then or the presumption is incompatible with the nature of the goods or the failure (section 19(15)).

Digital Services Act - 45 million figure: average monthly active recipients of the service in the Union equal to or higher than 45 million, for designation as very large online platforms or very large online search engines (Article 33(1)).

Digital Markets Act - 45 million figure: at least 45 million monthly active end users established or located in the Union in the last financial year, identified and calculated in accordance with the methodology and indicators set out in the Annex (Article 3(b)).

Digital Markets Act - additional requirement: alongside the 45 million monthly active end users, it requires at least 10 000 yearly active business users established in the Union in the last financial year (Article 3(b)), and that the thresholds in point (b) were met in each of the last three financial years (Article 3(c)).

The DSA counts average monthly active recipients of the service in the Union, while the DMA counts monthly active end users established or located in the Union; the DMA additionally requires at least 10 000 yearly active business users and that the thresholds were met in each of the last three financial years.
